title: Letting Go of the Past: EMDR
coreMove: EMDR treats traumatic memory as something that can process through anchored attention, bilateral stimulation, and association, with safety guiding pace over forced disclosure.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a strange origin story could be dismissed or oversold
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Francine Shapiro, late 1980s, eye movements, and EMDR without reducing the protocol to spectacle

exampleSpecs.stakes: a stuck assault memory could be forced into narration too soon
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a broken beer bottle assault shifting through EMDR processing rather than simple retelling

exampleSpecs.audience: supervisors working with complex developmental trauma
exampleSpecs.stakes: curiosity about abuse details could interrupt processing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use childhood sexual abuse, Brookline Trauma Center, and EMDR sessions to protect associative movement

exampleSpecs.audience: residents linking therapy to sleep research
exampleSpecs.stakes: a possible mechanism could harden into overclaim
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Robert Stickgold and REM-related memory consolidation as a possible explanation, not final proof

exampleSpecs.stakes: data could become either dismissal of medication or false certainty about EMDR
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Brookline Trauma Center findings on EMDR and medication for some PTSD patients

exampleSpecs.audience: therapists tempted to chase narrative detail
exampleSpecs.stakes: a patient's associative shift could be interrupted by the clinician's curiosity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the clinician following internal process rather than demanding every narrative detail
